issues.problem: The GAP item reads: 'GAP: 임직원 개인매매 사전승인 절차의 구체적 워크플로 — HF-REF-06 §4.5는 임직원 개인 매매 규정 제정 필요성만 언급함.' I grepped every chunk: the phrase 임직원 개인 매매 never appears in HF-REF-06 at all (§4.5's actual text covers 준법감시인 겸직 금지, 책무구조도, and common violation types — nothing about personal trading). The phrase only exists in HF-REF-08 표6-1 (CCO's job description) and HF-REF-18 표10-1 (the regulation checklist row). The cited section does not say what the item claims.
issues.correction: Re-cite this GAP to HF-REF-08 표 6-1 and/or HF-REF-18 표 10-1, not HF-REF-06 §4.5.

issues.problem: ir-lead-agent is said to support 'IR 전담 인력' with chunks:["HF-REF-11"]. HF-REF-11 (보수 구조/자금조달) never contains the phrase 'IR 전담 인력' — I read the full chunk and it is absent. The phrase is actually HF-REF-08 §6.3 표 6-2's 2단계 성장기 row ('전략 2~3개로 확장, 전담 리스크팀, IR 전담 인력, 기준가 내부 검증...').
issues.correction: Cite HF-REF-08 §6.3 표 6-2 for this item instead of (or in addition to) HF-REF-11.

issues.problem: cro-agent (전담 리스크팀 지원) is placed in the 3단계 기관화 (25명+) roster and quotes '전담 리스크팀', citing HF-REF-08 §6.3. But 표6-2 ties '전담 리스크팀' specifically to 2단계 성장기 (10~25명); the 3단계 기관화 row instead reads '복수 PM 체제, 중앙 리스크·데이터 플랫폼, 해외 펀드 구조 검토'. The quote is real but is being attached to the wrong growth-stage row.

issues.problem: owner is given as 'CIO(초안)/CCO(검증)'. orgverify.overall: The blueprint is largely well-sourced: I checked 58 distinct citation instances against the actual chunk text in /home/user/cgs/docs/hedge-fund-setup/ref/ (chunks 03, 05, 06, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 14, 16, 17, 18), and the great majority — including every load-bearing number I was asked to verify (3명, 10억원, 400%, 2주일, 5년, 5%/7.5%) — match the cited section exactly. The org-chart reporting lines (HF-REF-08 §6.2/§6.4), the independence rule (risk/compliance must not report to CIO), and all HF-REF-17 §9.5 표9-5 'principles' citations check out verbatim. Step 3/4 checks pass: every role the report ties to a statute has human_required=true with a real citation, no role lacks a stated basis without acknowledging it (INFERENCE/GAP labels are used honestly and accurately in the cases I checked, e.g. MNPI, ESG, and personal-data gaps are genuinely absent from all 21 chunks, confirmed by grep), and none of the three independence-sensitive control types (risk-vs-CIO, custody, valuation) are assigned to the CIO line. However, three citations are genuinely wrong — they point to a chunk/section that does not contain the claimed text (the '임직원 개인매매' GAP mis-cites HF-REF-06 §4.5 instead of HF-REF-08/18; 'IR 전담 인력' mis-cites HF-REF-11 instead of HF-REF-08 §6.3; and 'cro-agent 전담 리스크팀' is attached to the wrong growth-stage row). A handful of other fields state something as report fact without an INFERENCE tag when the chunks don't actually support it (핵심상품설명서's CCO-verifies claim contradicts the report's own '판매사가 검증' language; the model-governance control's '+ 퀀트 리드' co-ownership and the macro CIO/economist double-hat are both uncited additions). Finally, the blueprint silently drops several hard, numbered items straight out of 표4-3/표4-4/§6.5 (investor-count caps, the 15-year control-investment divestment rule, transfer restrictions, ad rules, the external-audit obligation, the 90-day/12-month securities-lending tenor cap, and the deferred performance-fee rule for larger firms) — none of these appear anywhere, not even flagged as a gap. Net: the blueprint survives verification on its core claims but should not be accepted as-is; the 3 wrong citations need re-pointing, the ~4 unsupported/uncited additions need an INFERENCE tag or removal, and the 7 missing regulatory items need to be added (at minimum as gaps) before this is used as the basis for T2 planning.

assessment.area: Management, meta and support skills (25 skills) — Strategy C transplant assessment for hedge-fund target
findings: This area has the highest pure-reuse rate of any component class reviewed so far: 15 of 25 skills (sprint-plan, sprint-status, retrospective, scope-check, settings, skill-test, skill-improve, estimate, milestone-review) carry zero or textually-inert game coupling and verify as TAKE with no required rewrite — well above the project-wide T2 baseline of 41.4% reuse, because project-management/meta tooling is inherently domain-agnostic.

gate-check is the single most cross-referenced skill in the entire 74-skill catalog (grep found it named by 34 other skill files, vs. the next-widest, sprint-plan, at 22). It must transplant early and be architecturally stable, since every hedge-fund domain skill written fresh will reference it from a 'next steps' section, exactly as it is referenced today.

sprint-plan, sprint-status, settings, project-stage-detect, adopt and start form a second-tier 'spine' (each referenced by 4-6 other skills) that should transplant in the same wave as the operating foundation (hooks, yaml-helper.sh, session-state) the founder already scoped for Strategy C, because domain skills not yet written will assume their commands exist.

Three components — bug-report, hotfix, tech-debt — score materially higher for a hedge fund than the mapping.txt T2 (knowledge-service agency) verdict suggests (T2 marks all three R = redesign/no-fit). The reason is structural, not cosmetic: a hedge fund, unlike a consulting/agency business, has a real, regulator-scrutinized code and model pipeline (OMS/EMS, risk engine, quant models), so game-studio bug-triage, incident-hotfix and tech-debt-register patterns are a closer structural match to a hedge fund than to an agency. day-one-patch and changelog show the same undervaluation for the same reason.

gate-check's own mechanism — verdict precedence (FAIL > CONCERNS > NOT ASSESSED > PASS), the explicit 'a check that cannot report it did not run is not a check' discipline, and Chain-of-Verification challenge questions — is the single highest-value transplant candidate in this area for the review's stated regulatory requirements (independent CCO/CRO reporting lines, numeric-rule enforcement, audit trail). But it cannot be finalized as TAKE-MODIFY without a founder decision: today's director-panel width is *tier-scalable* (1 director at minimal workflow, up to 4 at full) via `.claude/skills/gate-check/SKILL.md:390-400`, and if a CRO/CCO seat is mapped onto that same scaling mechanism without change, compliance/risk review becomes skippable by a `modes.workflow` or `modes.review_mode` setting — which a regulated entity cannot allow.

Cross-reference grep closes the transplant set for this area: within it, gate-check <- {milestone-review, retrospective, help, project-stage-detect, adopt, start}; sprint-plan <-> {sprint-status, scope-check, estimate, milestone-review, retrospective, help, tech-debt}; bug-report <-> {bug-triage, hotfix, day-one-patch}; changelog <-> patch-notes <-> {hotfix, day-one-patch}. Outside this area, all 25 skills reference into the game-domain skill catalog only in their 'Next Steps' / 'Follow-Up' sections (command names like /create-stories, /design-system, /architecture-decision) — none of the 25 read domain-skill *output formats* directly, so this area can transplant and function correctly before any hedge-fund domain skill exists; the domain skills, once written, will need to know these 25 skills' command names to link back.

All 25 T2 verdicts and their Korean rationale notes were transcribed correctly from mapping.txt, and the assessment correctly covers all 25 skills named in the area's scope with no missing components. The substantive verdict disagreements with T2 (upgrading bug-report, hotfix, tech-debt, changelog, and day-one-patch from R to TAKE-MODIFY, on the grounds that a hedge fund's real code/model pipeline makes SRE-style incident/change-control patterns more applicable than to a knowledge-service agency) are well-reasoned, internally consistent with the cited T2 rationale notes (several of which describe only minor game-terminology coupling despite an R verdict), and the proposed hedge-fund adaptations (adding a CRO/CCO approver to hotfix's sign-off, model-version stamping, etc.) are appropriate to a regulated, audit-trail-driven context. The gate-check CONDITIONAL flag and its silent-break analysis (director-panel width scaling with modes.workflow potentially letting a CRO/CCO review be skipped) is accurate and well-supported (SKILL.md:390-400, :484-490 verified) and is a genuinely important catch for a regulated entity. However, I confirmed four real problems, the most serious being a fabricated/inconsistent headline statistic: the claim that '15 of 25' skills are pure-TAKE with 'no required rewrite,' framed as 'well above' the 41.4% project-wide baseline, is wrong on every sub-part — only 8 of 25 are pure TAKE (32%, actually below the baseline), only 9 are even named, and one of those 9 (estimate) is itself TAKE-MODIFY with real listed changes. Second, the closing claim that 'none of the 25 read domain-skill output formats directly' is directly contradicted by the assessment's own descriptions of adopt (systems-index.md format audit) and consistency-check (entities.yaml + GDD parsing), undermining the conclusion that this area can transplant fully independent of any hedge-fund domain-skill output existing. Third, the 'spine' cross-reference bullet overstates mutuality: most of the 13 skill pairs asserted with bidirectional '<->' notation are actually one-directional per direct grep. Fourth, the specific gate-check/sprint-plan reference-count numbers (34/22) don't reproduce exactly and sprint-plan's claimed rank as runner-up is questionable against create-stories. None of these four issues invalidate the assessment's core recommendations, but the report's opening and closing framing bullets should be corrected before being relied on for sequencing/prioritization decisions.

assessment.area: Delivery-pipeline skills marked D or R for T2 (knowledge-service org) -- reassessed for a hedge-fund management company under two founder branches: (a) code-pipeline=no (document-centric fund), (b) code-pipeline=yes (quant research/backtests/signal code/model governance). 26 skills: architecture-decision, architecture-review, create-architecture, create-control-manifest, create-epics, create-stories, story-readiness, story-done, dev-story, code-review, test-setup, test-helpers, smoke-check, regression-suite, test-evidence-review, test-flakiness, security-audit, propagate-design-change, reverse-document, qa-plan, team-qa, team-release, release-checklist, launch-checklist, perf-profile, soak-test.
findings: All 26 skills were D/R for T2 for the same root reason: they assume a code-producing delivery pipeline (Decision Records governing implementation, engine-routed test evidence, code review) absent in a document/campaign knowledge-service org. A code-pipeline=yes quant archetype reintroduces that exact assumption, so most flip from LEAVE(a) to TAKE-MODIFY(b); only propagate-design-change and create-control-manifest are TAKE-MODIFY under BOTH branches, because their mechanism was already the least game-coupled in the original CCGS review (propagate-design-change was the ONLY skill in this batch rated T1=K, 'reusable as-is').

create-control-manifest is the highest-value regulatory-governance donor: its 'must-do/never-do rules extracted from Accepted decisions, versioned, staleness-checked against every downstream story' shape maps almost directly onto a Trading & Compliance Control Manifest carrying exposure limits, loss rules, and the 400% NAV leverage cap as its Global Guardrails section -- this directly operationalizes founder-brief item 2 (numeric rules).

The 'Story Type' taxonomy (Logic / Integration / Visual-Feel / UI / Config-Data) threads through 7 of the 26 skills (create-stories, dev-story, story-done, qa-plan, code-review, test-evidence-review, smoke-check). It needs ONE centrally-authored replacement taxonomy before any of the 7 are forked independently, or the fresh-authoring strategy risks silent cross-skill drift (see silent_breaks).

CCGS's Config/Data evidence-gate default is ADVISORY (non-blocking) in coding-standards.md and mirrored in create-stories, dev-story and story-done. For a hedge fund, 'Config/Data' is precisely a model-parameter change -- the class of change central to the 2025 SEC Two Sigma enforcement matter. Carrying the ADVISORY default over unmodified is a named governance risk; recommend flipping to BLOCKING for any code-pipeline=yes archetype (see founder_questions).

Several skills scored D purely because their literal CONTENT is engine-specific (test-setup's Godot/Unity/Unreal runners and CI YAML, test-helpers' GDScript/C#/C++ snippets, dev-story's game-role programmer-routing table, security-audit's Godot grep patterns) while their STRUCTURE and internal discipline (verification-not-inference, NOT-ASSESSED handling, freshness-checked context loading, quarantine-not-delete) is high-value and domain-general -- these are 'skeleton donors' per Strategy C, not direct transplants.

launch-checklist is the one skill in this batch the original review itself rated T2=R rather than D, despite being almost entirely game-specific line items -- its cross-departmental readiness structure (Code+Content+Legal+Infra+Community+Operations converging on one go/no-go with named sign-offs) is domain-general even though its content is not. This is the strongest single piece of evidence that hedge-fund reuse in this batch tracks skill SHAPE more than skill CONTENT.

No skill in this area covers 'code access control' (half of model-governance duty #3) at all -- this is a genuine content gap requiring fresh authoring, not a missed transplant; it slots naturally as a new Category 7 in a forked security-audit.

The dev-story skill (T1=R even in the original review, the most engine-coupled skill assessed) is the one skill where code-pipeline=no yields a clean, unqualified LEAVE with almost nothing worth donating beyond its context-freshness-check discipline, which lives more naturally inside story-done/story-readiness anyway.

issues.problem: Assessment claims propagate-design-change was 'the ONLY skill in this batch rated T1=K' (findings[0] and the component's own rationale). mapping.txt line 37 shows propagate-design-change's t1 value is W, not K. The assessment's own text elsewhere names create-epics and regression-suite as also T1=K (lines 18 and 41), so the 'ONLY' claim is both wrong against the source and self-contradictory within the same JSON.
issues.correction: Correct propagate-design-change's T1 rating to W; drop the 'ONLY T1=K' framing and re-derive the least-game-coupled/highest-confidence-donor argument from the actual T1=K set (create-epics, regression-suite, test-evidence-review).

issues.problem: Assessment calls launch-checklist 'the ONE skill in this batch the original review itself rated T2=R rather than D, despite being almost entirely game-specific line items' and treats this as 'the strongest single piece of evidence' for the report's shape-over-content thesis. mapping.txt shows 10 of the 26 skills are T2=R (create-epics, create-stories, story-readiness, story-done, test-evidence-review, qa-plan, team-qa, team-release, release-checklist, launch-checklist), including release-checklist, which per the assessment's own text carries comparably heavy game/platform-specific content (Steamworks/ESRB).
issues.correction: Remove the uniqueness claim; re-derive the shape-over-content argument from the full 10-skill T2=R set rather than resting the report's headline evidence on a false singularity.

issues.problem: Evidence cites create-epics/SKILL.md:91-104 with the quote 'minimal tier -- synthesize the epic from the brief ... Generate one coarse story per MVP feature.' This text does not exist anywhere in create-epics/SKILL.md (verified by grep). The quote is actually from create-stories/SKILL.md, lines ~91-99. create-epics's own minimal-tier behavior (lines 28-40) is simply 'optional, skipped' -- it has no such synthesis step of its own.
issues.correction: Re-cite as create-stories/SKILL.md:91-99, and correct the create-epics 'condition' field, which wrongly attributes the minimal-tier synthesis mechanism to create-epics itself.

issues.problem: The report generalizes the engine-specialist sub-agent spawn (dev-story, architecture-decision, architecture-review, create-architecture, code-review) as 'directly implementing independent validation, one of the five named model-governance duties,' describing it as 'distinct from the author.' For a regulated hedge fund this overstates the mechanism: the spawned specialist is a same-session sub-agent under the same operator's control, not an organizationally/reporting-line-independent reviewer, which is what segregation of duties requires -- a factor the verification brief explicitly asked to be checked.
issues.correction: Qualify these claims: the mechanism is at best a pre-screen that a real independent (human, differently-reporting-line) validator would still need to perform; it does not by itself satisfy segregation-of-duties / independent-validation requirements.

verify.overall: The assessment's evidence citations are almost entirely accurate: of ~52 checked against the actual files at their cited line ranges, only one (create-epics/SKILL.md:91-104) does not exist where claimed -- the quote is actually from create-stories/SKILL.md. All 26 named components exist in .claude/skills/ with the claimed SKILL.md/CONTRACT.md files present, and the assessment's component list fully covers the declared 26-skill scope (no missing components found). However, two of the report's headline, most-emphasized claims are factually wrong against its own cited ground-truth source (mapping.txt): (1) propagate-design-change is claimed to be 'the ONLY skill... rated T1=K,' but mapping.txt shows it is T1=W, and the assessment's own text elsewhere concedes create-epics and regression-suite are T1=K -- an internally self-contradictory, source-contradicted claim underpinning the report's central 'survives both branches' argument. (2) launch-checklist is claimed to be 'the ONE skill... rated T2=R despite being almost entirely game-specific,' called 'the strongest single piece of evidence' for the report's core thesis, but mapping.txt shows 10 of 26 skills are T2=R, including release-checklist, which the report itself describes as comparably game/platform-specific. Both of these are load-bearing rhetorical anchors (each appears twice, in both the top-level findings array and the specific component's rationale) and both fail verification against the source table the task instructed me to check them against. Separately, the report's repeated framing of same-session sub-agent specialist spawns as 'directly implementing independent validation' / a reviewer 'distinct from the author' overstates what the mechanism provides relative to genuine segregation-of-duties requirements in a regulated hedge fund -- a domain-fit gap rather than a citation error. Net: the assessment is evidentially solid at the citation level but its two strongest cross-cutting arguments rest on false uniqueness claims that should be corrected or withdrawn before this report is used to prioritize the migration.

findings: All 23 skills in this area resolve to hedge-fund verdict LEAVE (or CONDITIONAL where an in-house build decision gates the value), consistent with the task's framing — none of them transplant as literal skills, since a hedge fund has no game-design or game-team domain. Their value is entirely as skeleton donors, and the donor value varies widely by skill.

The single sharpest divergence from the T2 (agency) verdicts in this batch is /balance-check: T2 correctly rated it D (remove — an agency has no numeric game-formula domain to check), but for a hedge fund its dominant-strategy/'strictly better with no tradeoff' detection logic is one of the strongest donors in the whole review, because context point (2) (exposure limits, loss rules, 400%-of-NAV leverage cap) is exactly the numeric-rule domain this skill was built to police.

/design-system is the richest single donor: its 7-step Section Cycle (Context→Questions→Options→Decision→Draft→Approval→Write with unique-match Edit writes), its Category→Primary/Supporting-agent specialist-routing table, its Formulas variable-table format, and its Given-When-Then acceptance-criteria format together form a near-complete skeleton for an 'investment memo authoring' skill.

/design-review and /review-all-gdds together supply the two review-pipeline patterns the task asked for by name: parallel adversarial specialist review with a senior-synthesis step (design-review), and cross-document contradiction/economic-loop/multi-system-scenario-walkthrough analysis (review-all-gdds) — a near-direct donor pair for 'Investment Committee review' and 'cross-policy consistency review'.

/prototype and /vertical-slice supply two distinct PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL skeletons at two different rigor levels (cheap falsifiable-hypothesis test vs. full production-quality end-to-end dry run with a velocity log) — donors for a paper-trading pilot skill and an end-to-end investment-cycle dry run skill respectively, matching both requested examples in the task.

The seven team-* orchestration skills share one identical skeleton (Phase-0 config resolve, team.size-driven active-set collapse with a mandatory non-silent 'Active set' announcement, a three-part bounded write-exception, and an Error Recovery Protocol that verifies a named artifact actually exists on disk before treating a phase as done) — this shared skeleton, not any single skill's domain content, is the primary donor for the requested Investment Committee and Fund Launch team skills.

team-live-ops is the one team-* skill that already implements a real policy-compliance gate end-to-end (check output against `design/live-ops/ethics-policy.md`, block sign-off on a violation, require an explicit revise/override-with-documented-rationale/cancel decision, and flag plainly when the policy file does not even exist yet) — this is close to a direct donor, not just a skeleton, for the Investment Committee's compliance-check phase.

Every reviewed skill that emits a report/verdict follows `.claude/rules/skill-authoring.md` obligations 1–2 (NOT ASSESSED value; absent input never defaults to the permissive reading) with a worked example in asset-audit, balance-check, content-audit and ux-review — this pattern must be preserved verbatim, not simplified away, when any numeric or compliance-gate skill is rebuilt for the hedge fund, because a vacuous COMPLIANT/PASS against absent data or an uncommitted policy is disqualifying for a regulated entity in a way it is merely embarrassing for a game studio.

ux-design, ux-review, asset-spec and setup-engine are the four components marked CONDITIONAL rather than flat LEAVE — each has real donor value, but only if the founder decides the fund will build a specific piece of tooling in-house (investor portal/dashboard, marketing collateral pipeline, or a guided vendor/jurisdiction-selection skill); absent that decision they contribute nothing beyond what other higher-value donors already supply.

silent_breaks.symptom: At the default team.size=individual, control-function-equivalent agents (e.g. a CRO/CCO analogue) would silently route through the nearest core agent 'with an informational note' instead of being spawned — indistinguishable from a real independent review unless the reader specifically checks the 'Active set' line the skeleton requires.
silent_breaks.detection: Compare the printed Active-set announcement against a fixed, non-negotiable required-control-function list for the Investment Committee skill; treat any run missing CRO/CCO from that list as invalid, not merely lean.

silent_breaks.location: design-system.md:1047-1065 registry-conflict-check, if copied into an investment-memo skill's 'known facts locked' section without its absence/empty/present three-way guard
silent_breaks.symptom: design-system's own shipped template ships pre-populated example entries inside comments; its prescribed grep (`referenced_by.*[system-name]`) matches those comment lines on an empty registry, so the skill would present invented example numbers to the user as 'locked' facts. A rebuilt risk-limits or position-facts registry that copies the UI ('these values are locked') without copying this exact absence-handling logic will reproduce the same fabrication risk on real capital data.
silent_breaks.detection: When building the equivalent, explicitly test the empty-registry-with-commented-examples case before shipping — it is the state every new fund starts in.

silent_breaks.location: design-review.md:47-86 freshness/receipt skip, if reused for an investment-memo re-review skill
silent_breaks.symptom: CCGS measured that partial/delta re-reviews of an 'unchanged' document caught only 2 of 6 real defects a full review found, even with a forced whole-document scan step. If an IC memo review reuses the byte-identical-skip optimisation and hashes only the memo text (not the market/risk data it references), a memo whose referenced numbers are now stale (price moved, a limit changed) would report 'unchanged since last review, prior APPROVED verdict stands' on a live-capital decision.
silent_breaks.detection: Any hedge-fund reuse of this optimisation must hash the referenced market/risk-data inputs, not just the memo prose, or must not offer the skip at all for decisions gating live capital.

silent_breaks.location: team-live-ops.md:159-161 ethics-policy gate, if adapted for an IC compliance gate without porting its 'file does not exist' branch
silent_breaks.symptom: The donor pattern is good specifically because it names both failure modes (policy absent vs. policy violated). A naive port that keeps only the 'violation found → block' half and drops the 'policy file does not exist yet → flag and recommend creating one, do not silently pass' half would let a fund with no risk-limits document yet pass every IC review by default, on every trade, until someone happens to author the policy file — the exact 'reader with no writer defaults to the permissive branch on every run' failure `.claude/rules/skill-authoring.md` obligation 2 exists to catch.
silent_breaks.detection: Require the rebuilt gate to explicitly test 'policy file absent' as a first-class branch, not an afterthought, before it ships.

founder_questions.topic: Investment memo authoring rigor (design-system donor)
founder_questions.why: design-system's Section Cycle is the strongest single donor in this area for an investment-memo skill, but its full form (8 sections, mandatory specialist routing per category, a registry conflict-check) is scaled for a studio with many systems and many specialists — before it is rebuilt fresh, the memo's required depth needs to be pinned to how many strategies/PMs the fund will actually run at launch.
options: Full memo with mandatory CRO+quant+CCO specialist review for every position (mirrors design-system's `full` tier)
Lean 5-section memo, specialist review only above a position-size or risk-budget threshold (mirrors `standard` tier)
One-page memo, no formal specialist gate at launch — add later as headcount grows (mirrors the `minimal`/game-brief tier)
Defer the whole memo skill for the first months — rely on existing IC minutes / verbal process, revisit once trade volume justifies automation

founder_questions.topic: Control-function independence vs. team-size auto-collapse (team-* skeleton donor)
founder_questions.why: Every team-* skill defaults to team.size=individual, which silently routes named specialists through the nearest core agent instead of spawning them (identical pattern in all seven files, e.g. team-combat.md:40-44). Reusing this default unmodified for an Investment Committee skill would let CRO/CCO-equivalent review collapse into the CIO-equivalent agent by default — directly contradicting the segregation-of-duties requirement (context point 5).
options: Hard-code CRO and CCO as always-spawned, non-collapsible roles in the IC skill regardless of team.size
Disallow team.size=individual for the IC skill specifically — minimum floor is 'small'
Keep the collapse mechanism but require an explicit, logged founder-level override every time CRO/CCO would be skipped
Do not reuse the team.size lever at all for control functions — redesign the IC skill's agent selection from scratch

founder_questions.topic: Paper-trading pilot PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL signal (prototype donor)
founder_questions.why: /prototype's falsifiable-hypothesis + structured debrief + KILL-checklist mechanism (prototype.md:76-90, 375-399, 477-487) is a clean skeleton donor for a pre-launch paper-trading pilot, but the game skill's PROCEED signal is a human's subjective 'did it feel fun' — a hedge fund needs an objective, ideally backtestable, threshold instead before this can be rebuilt.
options: Define PROCEED as a quantitative Sharpe/drawdown/hit-rate threshold computed automatically from pilot P&L data
Keep it qualitative like the game version — PM judgment, formalized only by an IC sign-off vote
Two-stage gate: an automatic quantitative screen first, then a qualitative IC discussion only if the screen passes
Skip the formal paper-trading gate entirely — go straight to small live capital with a hard stop-loss instead

founder_questions.topic: Investor-collateral / marketing pipeline (asset-spec, asset-audit, ux-design, ux-review — the four CONDITIONAL components)
founder_questions.why: T2 (the agency comparison) kept asset-spec nearly as-is because content production is its actual business; for a hedge fund the same donor (sequential asset-ID scheme + shared-asset dedup, asset-spec.md:325-335 and :339-349) is only worth building if investor-facing materials (pitch deck, tear sheet, DDQ visuals, an investor portal) are produced in-house rather than outsourced.
options: Build a lightweight investor-collateral spec+audit pair now (pitch deck, tear sheet, one-pager) using these skills as the donor skeleton
Defer entirely — outsource all investor collateral and any investor-facing UI to an external design/IR firm
Build it later, contingent on AUM and a separate founder decision round about marketing/IR strategy
Not needed at all — investor materials will stay ad hoc with no formal spec/audit pipeline

verify.overall:
Adversarial verification of the "skills-design" (23-skill) assessment. Method: checked 56 of the assessment's evidence citations against the actual files at cited line ranges (+/-3 lines tolerance), cross-checked all T1/T2 verdict-code citations ("mapping.txt:N") against the real mapping.txt rows, re-derived the true scope of "design-domain and team skills in .claude/skills/" via ls/glob + coupling-column analysis, and spot-verified one checkable external fact via web search.

CITATIONS: All 56 checked quotes are verbatim-accurate (word-for-word or ellipsis-joined-verbatim) at or within a few lines of the cited range. Zero wrong citations found. This includes the highest-stakes ones: the design-system.md:1044-1068 registry-conflict-check citation was independently verified against the actual shipped design/registry/entities.yaml — it genuinely ships with `constants: []` (present-but-empty) followed by commented example entries containing exactly `gold_carry_limit: 9999` and `base_inventory_slots: 20`, confirming the silent_breaks fabrication-risk claim is real, not overstated. All 23 "mapping.txt:N" verdict-code citations (t1/t2 letters and coupling) were checked against the actual mapping.txt rows and all matched exactly.

VERDICT LOGIC: Of the 23 components, 8 have a T1≠T2 verdict in mapping.txt (balance-check, playtest-report, ux-design, ux-review, setup-engine, team-narrative, team-polish, team-ui). All 8 are explicitly explained in the assessment, and in every case the stated hedge-fund rationale is a reasonable, internally consistent application of the regulated/numeric-limits/audit-trail/segregation-of-duties context — no contradictions found. One specific external factual claim ("the 2025 SEC Two Sigma case turned on inadequate change-approval/review process") was independently verified via web search: the SEC's settled charges against Two Sigma were in fact announced/finalized in 2025 (civil penalties paid January 16, 2025) and did center on unauthorized, unsupervised changes to investment models — the claim is accurate, not an error (my initial suspicion that it should read "2023" was wrong; 2023 was only the internal-investigation/repayment period).

MISSING COMPONENTS: The assessment's own scope title claims "(23 skills)" as if it were the complete design-domain + team-orchestration set, but ls/glob plus coupling-column analysis of mapping.txt turned up four skills in the same categories that were silently omitted: (1) consistency-check and (2) quick-design — both in the same "시스템 설계" phase group with the same C/C,P coupling as design-review and design-system, which the assessment covers in depth — and (3) team-release and (4) team-qa — two of the nine team-* orchestrator files in .claude/skills/, of which the assessment only covers seven. Direct reads of team-release and team-qa confirm both share, verbatim in structure, the exact "Phase 0 config-resolve / Active-set announcement / bounded write-exception / Error Recovery Protocol" skeleton that the assessment's own headline finding (findings bullet 6, reuse_patterns entry 6) attributes to "the seven team-* orchestration skills" — meaning that specific count claim is verifiably wrong; the true figure is nine. This is the most consequential finding: it doesn't just omit two donor candidates, it makes an incorrect quantitative claim in the assessment's own summary.

No other unsupported (non-INFERENCE) factual claims were found to be wrong. No wrong-verdict issues were confirmed among the divergent components.

assessment.area: Agents, coordination, and director gates — CCGS → hedge-fund (Strategy C) feasibility
findings: mapping.txt (scratchpad) has NO per-agent breakdown — only aggregate counts for the 49 agents: T1 {K:16,W:9,R:19,D:5}, T2 {K:2,W:19,R:0,D:28} (review.txt:219 JSON block). All per-agent hedge-fund verdicts below are therefore new analysis, not a re-labeling of an existing per-agent T2 row; comparisons to T2 are made at the aggregate level or via the 28-row director-gate table (review.txt / mapping.txt lines 123-151), which DOES give per-gate T1/T2 verdicts.

Every one of the 28 director-gate definition files was read in full. director-gates.md:123-135 asserts 'All gates return one of three verdicts... Skills must handle all three' (APPROVE/READY, CONCERNS, REJECT/NOT READY), but the 28 files actually use at least 9 distinct verdict vocabularies: APPROVE/CONCERNS/REJECT (most CD-*, TD-*, AD-ART-BIBLE, AD-VISUAL, LP-CODE-REVIEW, ND-CONSISTENCY); READY/CONCERNS/NOT READY (the 4 PHASE-GATEs); REALISTIC/OPTIMISTIC/UNREALISTIC (pr-scope.md:25, unique — no other gate has an 'OPTIMISTIC' tier); REALISTIC/CONCERNS/UNREALISTIC (pr-sprint.md:24, pr-epic.md:30); ON TRACK/AT RISK/OFF TRACK (pr-milestone.md:24); VIABLE/CONCERNS/HIGH RISK (td-feasibility.md:24); FEASIBLE/CONCERNS/INFEASIBLE (lp-feasibility.md:23); ADEQUATE/GAPS/INADEQUATE (ql-story-ready.md:27, ql-test-coverage.md:23); and CONCEPTS/STRONG/CONCERNS (ad-concept-visual.md:25) — which has NO blocking tier at all. A caller that greps for the literal string 'REJECT' to decide whether to halt will silently pass every one of these other 8 gates' actual stop signal.

The director-gate 'blocking' behaviour described in director-gates.md:127-135 ('REJECT / NOT READY -> Do not write files or advance stage until resolved') is enforced only by the calling skill's own prose instructions to the LLM, not by any hook or permission check. .claude/docs/effects-map.md:1230-1245 states outright that `strict_gate_checks` — the config key that would formalize blocking vs advisory — is 'RESERVED - NOT IMPLEMENTED... No skill or hook reads this setting. Setting it has no effect.' gate-check/SKILL.md:604-623 confirms the actual stage-advance write happens only 'When the verdict is PASS and the user confirms' — i.e. a human-in-the-loop convention, not a code-enforced lock.

The ONE mechanism in this whole area that IS technically (harness-)enforced, not merely advisory, is the `tools: Agent(sub1, sub2, ...)` allow-list. Exactly 3 of 49 agents use it: godot-specialist.md:4, unity-specialist.md:4, unreal-specialist.md:4, each restricting the lead to spawning only its own named sub-specialists. godot-specialist.md:154-158 states explicitly: 'your tools: grant names exactly which ones -- you cannot spawn outside that set. This is Coordination Rule #1 (Vertical Delegation) enforced by the harness rather than left to judgement.' review.txt:185 confirms independently that renaming a sub-specialist without updating this list makes 'the harness block calling the new-named agent' — a loud, not silent, failure.

There are exactly three top-level 'Collaboration Protocol' variants across the 49 agents, matching the review's own claim (review.txt:147: '에이전트 골격(협업 프로토콜 3종)... 복사해 쓸 수 있습니다'): (1) 'Strategic Decision Workflow' / 'highest-level consultant' — creative-director.md:18-20, technical-director.md:14-16, producer.md:15-17 (3 agents, all Opus Tier-1); (2) 'Implementation Workflow' / 'collaborative implementer' — 34 agents including lead-programmer.md:16-18, security-engineer.md:10-12, qa-lead.md:18-20, release-manager.md:15-17, community-manager.md:11-13, devops-engineer.md:13-15, godot-specialist.md:10-12, analytics-engineer.md:13-15; (3) 'Question-First Workflow' / 'collaborative consultant' — 10 agents: art-director, audio-director, economy-designer, game-designer, level-designer, live-ops-designer, narrative-director, systems-designer, ux-designer, world-builder. Two files are hybrids the review's '3종' count glosses over: writer.md:17-19 carries variant-2's heading text but variant-3's 'Draft based on user's choice (incremental file writing)' step content; prototyper.md:50-66 shares only the opening sentence with variant 2 and otherwise has a unique 5-step protocol tailored to disposable builds.

Agent frontmatter field usage across all 49 (.claude/agents/*.md): name/description/tools/model/maxTurns on all 49; disallowedTools on 15 (grep -l disallowedTools, all = 'Bash', all non-programmer creative/design/comms roles); memory on 17 (`project` on 14, `user` on 3: creative-director, producer, technical-director); skills: [...] on 6 (creative-director, game-designer, lead-programmer, producer, qa-lead, release-manager); isolation: worktree on 1 (prototyper.md:7, unique); model values: inherit=30, sonnet=14, opus=3 (creative-director, technical-director, producer), haiku=2 (community-manager.md:5, devops-engineer.md:5).

model-tiers.md:3-21 and coordination-rules.md:20-24 (verbatim restated in CLAUDE.md) state a skill's `model:` frontmatter is measured, confirmed-unenforced ('Claude Code reads model: from a skill's frontmatter and then serves the skill from the session's model anyway'). The agent-side `model:` mechanism is explicitly different and explicitly UNVERIFIED in either direction: 'It has not been measured here, so treat the agent section below as unverified... rather than assuming it behaves the same way' (model-tiers.md:18-21). This matters directly for hedge-fund reuse: community-manager (IR-role donor) and devops-engineer both pin `model: haiku` — the cheapest tier — and that pin's real-world effect is unconfirmed.

The 28-gate T1/T2 verdict table (mapping.txt lines 123-151) shows T2 (knowledge-service) deleted (D, 'no counterpart') every code-governance gate: TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY, TD-ARCHITECTURE, TD-ADR, TD-MANIFEST, LP-FEASIBILITY, LP-CODE-REVIEW — because a marketing/consulting org has no code. A quant hedge fund (archetype=quant, code-pipeline=yes) is the opposite case from T2 here: it DOES have code (trading signals/execution), and the 2025 SEC Two Sigma case (named in task context) is precisely a model-change-control/code-access-control/version-history failure — so these same 6 gates, T2-deleted, come back as CONDITIONAL/TAKE-MODIFY for the hedge fund, reviving exactly what a generic-knowledge-service transplant would have discarded. This is the single largest reuse divergence between the T2 assessment and the hedge-fund one.

Conversely, all CD-*/AD-*/ND-CONSISTENCY creative-and-visual gates that T2 mostly KEPT (CD-PILLARS K/K, CD-PHASE-GATE K/K, AD-CONCEPT-VISUAL W/K, AD-PHASE-GATE W/K, AD-VISUAL W/K — because a content/marketing agency still needs brand-identity gates) are LEAVE for the hedge fund: a regulated asset manager has no comparable 'brand pillar stress test' or 'art bible sign-off' need in its core operating loop (a thin IR/marketing-collateral consistency check could exist later but is not part of the control framework).

coordination-rules.md:7-9 ('Conflict Resolution: escalate to the shared parent... if no shared parent, escalate to creative-director for design conflicts or technical-director for technical conflicts') already models two co-equal, mutually-independent Tier-1 escalation lanes with no subordination between them. This is structurally the closest existing pattern to the CRO/CCO-must-not-report-to-CIO requirement, but it is not sufficient as-is: nothing in the current rule set says an agent's output may NOT be overridden or edited by a peer director, and rule 5 ('No Unilateral Cross-Domain Changes... without explicit delegation') only protects file directories, not review authority — a hedge-fund CRO/CCO independence rule needs a new, explicit non-override clause this file does not currently express.

The `modes.review_mode` default is `lean` (director-gates.md:75: '`lean`| PHASE-GATEs only (`/gate-check`) — per-skill gates skipped. **Default**'). Under the inherited default, every fine-grained per-skill gate — including the code-governance gates above and any future CRO/CCO per-decision gate modeled the same way — is skipped by default; only the 4 phase-gate panel checks at stage transitions run. A hedge-fund fork that does not explicitly override this default ships with most of its 'director gate' compliance surface silently off.

Only 2 of the 49 agents (`community-manager`, `devops-engineer`) pin `model: haiku` in their own frontmatter (grep confirmed) — agent-roster.md additionally lists `qa-tester` and `accessibility-specialist` as Haiku, which is incorrect against the actual frontmatter (both are `model: inherit`); this exact discrepancy is independently flagged in review.txt:200, confirming it is a real, pre-existing doc/frontmatter mismatch in CCGS, not an artifact of this analysis.

silent_breaks.symptom: If a hedge-fund fork renames a sub-specialist (e.g. a future 'quant-platform-specialist' delegating to 'backtest-engine-specialist') without updating the lead agent's tools: Agent(...) list in the same edit, the harness refuses the spawn outright.
silent_breaks.change: Renaming/adding domain sub-specialist agents during the fresh domain-agent build under Strategy C
silent_breaks.detection: Loud, not silent — an immediate tool-permission error at spawn time (review.txt:185 confirms this is the one item on the original 13-point list classified '시끄러움'/loud rather than '조용함'/quiet).

silent_breaks.symptom: A founder who sets `strict_gate_checks: true` (or writes a hedge-fund-specific equivalent key by analogy) believing it makes a CRO/CCO REJECT verdict a hard stop gets no such effect — the value is validated for spelling and then ignored; no skill or hook reads it (effects-map.md:1240, 1245).
silent_breaks.change: Reusing the existing config-flag pattern to try to make a compliance gate 'blocking' by setting a project.yaml value, instead of building real enforcement
silent_breaks.detection: Silent — the flag round-trips cleanly through /settings, looks configured, and produces no observable difference in behavior.

silent_breaks.symptom: Even where a gate's own verdict word IS the documented 'blocking' one (REJECT/NOT READY/INFEASIBLE/etc.), nothing in the codebase prevents the orchestrating skill or a differently-behaving future skill from proceeding anyway — the stop is an instruction the LLM is told to follow ('Do not write files or advance stage until resolved'), not a permission-system check. If a hedge-fund pre-trade compliance or leverage-cap check is built the same way (a spawned CRO agent returning a text verdict that a calling skill is merely instructed to honor), a careless or adversarially-prompted run can silently execute a trade or advance state past a real limit breach with no technical error at all.
silent_breaks.change: Modeling the new CRO/CCO hard-block gates on the existing director-gate verdict pattern instead of on a hook
silent_breaks.detection: Silent under normal operation; only visible via after-the-fact audit-trail review, if one exists.

silent_breaks.symptom: With the inherited default, every per-skill director gate is skipped and only the 4 PHASE-GATEs run at stage transitions. If the hedge-fund fork copies this default forward, a CRO/CCO per-decision gate built the same way (i.e. invoked the way TD-ADR or LP-CODE-REVIEW are invoked today) is OFF by default from day one, with no error — the calling skill just prints '[GATE-ID] skipped — Lean mode' (director-gates.md:96-97) and proceeds.
silent_breaks.change: Standing up per-decision CRO/CCO gates using the existing review_mode-gated invocation pattern without separately hard-wiring them to always run regardless of review_mode
silent_breaks.detection: Silent unless someone is watching the skill's own transcript for the 'skipped — Lean mode' note; nothing downstream distinguishes a skipped gate from an approved one in most surfaces.

silent_breaks.location: 28 files under .claude/docs/director-gates/ (9 distinct verdict-vocabulary sets; enumerated in findings)
silent_breaks.symptom: director-gates.md:125 claims a single standard 3-tier vocabulary a caller can pattern-match against generically. In fact PR-SCOPE uses REALISTIC/OPTIMISTIC/UNREALISTIC, PR-MILESTONE uses ON TRACK/AT RISK/OFF TRACK, TD-FEASIBILITY uses VIABLE/CONCERNS/HIGH RISK, LP-FEASIBILITY uses FEASIBLE/CONCERNS/INFEASIBLE, QL-* uses ADEQUATE/GAPS/INADEQUATE, and AD-CONCEPT-VISUAL uses CONCEPTS/STRONG/CONCERNS with no blocking tier at all. A generic hedge-fund gate-verdict parser written against the documented 'standard' (grep for REJECT/NOT READY) will silently treat every one of these other verdicts as a non-blocking pass-through.
silent_breaks.change: Building new hedge-fund gates (or a generic verdict-checking helper) against director-gates.md's documented 'Standard Verdict Format' instead of against the actual per-gate files
silent_breaks.detection: Silent — the mismatched verdict string simply fails to match the block-condition and the workflow continues.

reuse_patterns.source: coordination-rules.md:7-9 (Conflict Resolution: two co-equal, non-subordinate Tier-1 escalation lanes — creative-director for design conflicts, technical-director for technical conflicts, neither reporting to the other)

founder_questions.topic: Trading/quant archetype and internal code pipeline
founder_questions.why: Determines whether the entire code-governance agent stack and its director gates (TD-SYSTEM-BOUNDARY, TD-ARCHITECTURE, TD-ADR, TD-MANIFEST, LP-FEASIBILITY, LP-CODE-REVIEW, QL-TEST-COVERAGE — all 'D'/deleted for the generic T2 knowledge-service target per mapping.txt) should be revived for the hedge fund, or left out entirely. This is the single largest branch point in the agents/gates area.
options: Quant/systematic — internal signal & execution code exists; build the full model-governance stack (code review, version history, change approval) per the SEC Two Sigma precedent
Discretionary only — no internal trading/model code; skip the entire code-governance agent and gate family
Hybrid — internal quant research only (no live execution code); reuse prototyper's isolation pattern for a research sandbox but skip production code-review gates
Undecided — stand up the CRO/CCO/CIO control core now and revisit the dev-stack question before Technical Setup stage

founder_questions.topic: Enforcement mechanism for hard-blocking controls (pre-trade compliance, leverage cap, limit breach)
founder_questions.why: CCGS's existing director-gate verdict system is advisory in a technical sense — a spawned agent's REJECT/NOT READY text verdict is honored only because the calling skill's prose tells the orchestrating agent to honor it, and the one config key that would make gate failures formally blocking (`strict_gate_checks`) is documented as reserved and unimplemented (effects-map.md:1230-1245). A regulated fund's pre-trade and limit checks cannot rely on an LLM agent choosing to comply.
options: Build a new PreToolUse hook (same class of mechanism as validate-commit.sh, hooks-reference.md:7) that hard-blocks any trade/order tool call breaching a configured limit, independent of any agent's verdict
Accept the advisory pattern for now (agent verdict + mandatory human sign-off before any order is placed) and add hook-based enforcement once the actual trade-execution tool surface is defined
Require human approval on every single order regardless of any agent verdict until hook-based enforcement is built and tested
Other — describe the intended enforcement point

founder_questions.topic: CRO/CCO reporting-line independence — exact rule to encode
founder_questions.why: coordination-rules.md's existing escalation model (creative-director / technical-director as co-equal, non-subordinate Tier-1 escalation targets) is structurally close to what CRO/CCO independence needs, but nothing in the current rule set prevents a peer director from overriding or editing another director's output — only file-directory ownership is protected (rule 5). The exact independence guarantee needs to be specified before the coordination rules can be rewritten.
options: CRO and CCO are co-equal Tier-1 roles alongside CIO/COO, each with an independent escalation lane that bypasses CIO entirely (direct extension of the existing creative-director/technical-director pattern)
CRO and CCO report only to the Board/founder, never to CIO or COO, plus a new explicit rule that no CIO-side agent may edit or override CRO/CCO gate output
A single unified 'control function' Tier-1 agent covering both risk and compliance, kept independent of CIO only (simpler, but conflates two functions regulators usually expect to be separable)
Not decided yet — needs to be modeled/drafted before founder can choose

founder_questions.topic: Trust level for the agent-side `model:` pin on compliance-/investor-facing roles
founder_questions.why: model-tiers.md and coordination-rules.md both state that while skill-level `model:` is confirmed unenforced, agent-level `model:` is explicitly unverified in either direction ('untested, not known-broken'). Two of the strongest hedge-fund skeleton donors identified — community-manager (→ IR) and devops-engineer — currently pin `model: haiku`, the cheapest tier, and it is unknown whether that pin will actually govern the model used for investor-facing or infrastructure-security work once transplanted.
options: Test whether agent-level `model:` pinning actually takes effect before launch, then set tiers deliberately per role
Don't rely on the model: field at all — control model choice at the orchestrator/session level instead
Pin every control-function and investor-facing agent to the highest available tier regardless of cost, since the mechanism is unverified
Not a launch blocker — defer and revisit post-launch

verify.overall:
Checked 62 of the assessment's evidence citations (well beyond the 49 agents + 28 gates it covers) by opening each cited file at the given line. The large majority -- all agent-description quotes (20/20 checked), all 28 gate files' Verdicts lines (used to confirm the '9 distinct vocabularies' claim, which is exactly right: 28 files split 15/4/1/2/1/1/1/2/1 across 9 vocabularies), all frontmatter counts (disallowedTools=15, memory=17, skills:=6, isolation:=1, model tiers 30/14/3/2), the tools:Agent(...) harness-enforcement claim (independently confirmed via validate-commit.sh's real exit-2 blocking behavior and the CD/TD/PR agent-tier structure in agent-roster.md), and the mapping.txt gate-verdict-table citations (CD-PILLARS K/K, AD-CONCEPT-VISUAL W/K, code-governance gates K/D, PR-* K/K, aggregate agent counts) -- check out exactly as quoted, with correct file:line references. This is a well-researched, carefully cited assessment.

However genuine problems survived verification. (1) Four of the 28 director gates -- TD-ENGINE-RISK, TD-CHANGE-IMPACT, TD-FEASIBILITY, QL-STORY-READY -- never receive a hedge-fund component verdict, and two of them are never mentioned at all, directly contradicting the assessment's own claim to have read all 28 gate files in full; TD-ENGINE-RISK is a materially relevant omission given the report's central SEC-Two-Sigma/code-governance argument. (2) The '2025 SEC Two Sigma case' is used as load-bearing justification for the report's single largest divergence claim, but its factual characterization is asserted as settled fact in two of its three appearances and hedged as task-context only once -- this could not be confirmed against the repo. (3) Three citations are demonstrably wrong on direct inspection: 'review.txt:219' for the JSON counts block (that line doesn't exist in review.txt; it's mapping.txt:219), the claim that review.txt:185 is 'the one' item marked loud among 13 silent-break candidates (it's actually 1 of 3), and a misattributed T2-rationale phrase for ND-CONSISTENCY that actually belongs to a different gate, CD-NARRATIVE. (4) The claim that all 15 disallowedTools agents are 'non-programmer creative/design/comms roles' is false for one of them, ue-blueprint-specialist. None of these overturn the assessment's core structural conclusions (the tools:Agent(...) mechanism is genuinely harness-enforced; the director-gate verdict system genuinely is advisory-only; the T2-vs-hedge-fund divergence on code-governance gates is a real and defensible reuse pattern), but they are real, checkable defects that should be corrected before the founder-facing plan is finalized.

findings: DELIVERABLE 1 SUMMARY -- workflow-catalog.yaml (.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml:1-427): schema is `phases:` -> dict of phase-id -> {label, description, next_phase, steps:[{id, name, command, required(bool), repeatable(bool), description, artifact:{glob, pattern, min_count(default 1), note, any_of:[{glob,pattern}]}}]} (lines 1-19 document the schema in comments). The 7 phases in next_phase order are concept(5 steps)->systems-design(4)->technical-setup(5)->pre-production(11)->production(9)->polish(5)->release(4). Two consumers were read directly: (a) .claude/scripts/artifact-check.sh is a hand-rolled indentation-walking parser (no PyYAML dependency, by design) that evaluates each step's glob/pattern(POSIX ERE via grep -E)/min_count/any_of against disk and prints ONLY observations (PRESENT/ABSENT/SHORT/PATTERN_MISS/NO_CHECK/UNKNOWN) -- its header explicitly cites 'context-management.md rule 2' (scripts emit observations, never verdicts), the same rule CLAUDE.md restates; (b) .claude/skills/help/SKILL.md Step 1 (line 37) reads the catalog as authoritative, Step 1b Globs installed skills and diffs against catalog `command:` values to surface uncataloged skills, Step 4 shells to `artifact-check.sh --phase [current-phase]` and maps its 5 statuses to Complete/Incomplete/MANUAL/UNKNOWN. .claude/skills/gate-check/SKILL.md runs the identical script scoped to the source phase and layers the required/optional + workflow-tier judgment on top.

DELIVERABLE 1, INFERENCE on two tracks -- whether the schema supports a firm-setup track and an investment-operations track without code change: NO, not fully, and this is VERIFIED by reading the consumers, not assumed. The YAML SHAPE needs no change (phases: is a flat id-keyed dict; investment-ops phase ids could sit alongside firm-setup phase ids, each with its own next_phase chain). But the STATE-TRACKING code assumes exactly one active phase: /help SKILL.md Step 2 (lines 96-105) hardcodes a single 7-row Concept->...->Release name-to-key lookup table against one scalar project.stage, and /gate-check writes that same scalar. A two-track project needs either two stage scalars or a track dimension in project.yaml, PLUS edits to /help's Step 2 table and /gate-check's stage-write logic -- both are skill-file changes, not YAML-schema changes.

DELIVERABLE 4 -- Skill Testing Framework's four modes, evidence-based. STATIC (`/skill-test static [name|all]`): reads only .claude/skills/[name]/SKILL.md, runs 7 structural checks, produces COMPLIANT/NON-COMPLIANT. Works even with the whole framework folder deleted (README.md:17). SPEC (`/skill-test spec [name]`): reads catalog.yaml's spec: path, reads the spec file (5 test cases: Happy Path/Failure-Blocked/Mode Variant/Edge Case/Director Gate), verdict PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL. BREAKS without the folder (README.md:19). CATEGORY (`/skill-test category [name|all]`): reads quality-rubric.md, scores 4-5 binary PASS/FAIL/WARN metrics for the matching category, verdict COMPLIANT/WARNINGS/NON-COMPLIANT. BREAKS without the folder. AUDIT (`/skill-test audit`): enumerates all skills/agents, cross-checks catalog.yaml's spec: field, produces a coverage table, verdict COMPLETE. DEGRADES without the folder (README.md:18, 'reports that no catalog exists').

DELIVERABLE 4 -- what catalog.yaml holds (read in full): `version: 2`, `last_updated`, then `skills:` (74 entries, verified by grep -c split at the agents: boundary) each with {name, spec(path), last_static, last_static_result, last_spec, last_spec_result, last_category, last_category_result, priority(critical/high/medium/low), category}, then `agents:` (49 entries) each with {name, spec, last_spec, last_spec_result, category}. 74+49=123, matching the review's own '123' figure exactly -- now directly verified. Two entries have spec: "" (vertical-slice, settings) -- a real gap even within CCGS itself.

DELIVERABLE 4 -- quality-rubric.md criteria quoted per category (full file read). gate: 'G1 - Review mode read | Skill reads production/session-state/review-mode.txt ... before deciding which directors to spawn' / 'G5 - No auto-advance | Skill never writes production/stage.txt without explicit user confirmation'. review: 'R3 - Correct verdict vocabulary | Verdict is exactly one of: APPROVED / NEEDS REVISION / MAJOR REVISION NEEDED (design) or PASS / CONCERNS / FAIL (architecture)'. authoring: 'A5 - Skeleton-first | Full authoring skills create a file skeleton with all section headers before filling content'. readiness: 'RD3 - BLOCKED requires external action | reserved for issues that cannot be fixed by the story author alone'. pipeline: 'P3 - May-I-write before each artifact | not batch-approving all files at once'. analysis: 'AN1 - Read-only scan | uses only Read/Glob/Grep tools; no Write or Edit during the scan itself' and 'AN3 - No auto-write | gated behind May I write'. team: 'T3 - BLOCKED surfacing | surfaces it immediately and halts dependent work -- never silently skips'. sprint: 'SP4 - No auto-commit | never writes sprint files or milestone records without May I write'. utility: 'U1 - Passes all 7 static checks'. director: 'D1 - Returns APPROVE / CONCERNS / REJECT' and 'D4 - Opus model tier'. lead: 'L2 - Escalates to shared parent'. specialist: 'S3 - Defers correctly | redirected to the correct agent, not refused silently'. engine: 'E1 - Version-aware | flags post-cutoff risk'. qa: 'Q3 - No scope creep | flags gaps for humans to decide'. operations: 'O2 - Defers implementation | delegates to appropriate specialist'.

DELIVERABLE 4 -- what must change when all skill/agent names change: FOUR files enumerate the same 123 names and must be rewritten in lockstep: (1) catalog.yaml's 74+49 name:/spec: pairs; (2) quality-rubric.md's 9 skill-category and 6 agent-category named lists (e.g. line 16 'Skills: gate-check'); (3) CLAUDE.md lines 28-68's two ASCII tables; (4) README.md lines 111-136's two tables. If only the skill files are renamed and these registries are left stale: audit mode reports every new HF skill as 'no spec', spec mode has no catalog entry to resolve, category mode has no matching rubric list for a new category. This corroborates, with mechanism now verified, the review's 30-90 hour estimate to rewrite 123 behavioral specs, and adds that the 4 registry files are a separate, smaller rewrite pass that must happen first since spec/category modes are catalog-driven lookups.

DELIVERABLE 4 -- proposed AAA acceptance bar for new hedge-fund skills/agents: (1) floor = static mode 0-FAIL (U1) plus skill-authoring.md's five obligations, most load-bearing being obligation 1 (a could-not-assess value that outranks pass) and obligation 3 (a skipped step announces itself in the output); (2) control-function agents (CCO/CRO-equivalent) must satisfy D1+D4 plus a strengthened D3 that routes an unresolved compliance escalation outside the investment chain entirely (to the board/external compliance officer) rather than to the CIO -- a genuinely NEW criterion, not a reuse; (3) compliance/risk monitoring skills must satisfy AN1+AN3 as a hard BLOCKING gate, not the ADVISORY default T1/T2 analysis skills get, since a compliance check that can silently skip is the SEC Two Sigma failure mode; (4) any skill recording an investment decision/trade/model change must satisfy P3+P5 and RD3's BLOCKED-requires-external-action distinction; (5) all must pass a real failing-gate test per skill-authoring.md's closing rule ('break the thing it guards, confirm it fails, restore') before being marked AAA-compliant -- a process requirement to write into the HF framework's own audit checklist.

T2-COMPARISON, most consequential divergence: T2's own verdicts (mapping.txt) treat ADR-related templates and gameplay-code.md as D across the board, with the calibration note stating T2 does not write ADRs. For a hedge fund with a quant/code archetype this is backwards: ADRs and 'never hardcode, always externally configured' are directly what the SEC Two Sigma model-governance failure (context point 3) demands. A T2-style verdict pass taken uncritically would strip exactly the components a hedge fund's control functions rely on most. HF is not simply 'T2 but regulated' -- on the code/model-governance axis it is closer to T1, even though on the domain-content axis it is much closer to T2's near-total D-and-R pattern. This report's component verdicts reflect that split explicitly rather than defaulting to either prior verdict set.

issues.problem: The workflow-catalog.yaml component's evidence array cites '.claude/skills/help/SKILL.md' lines 96-105 for the quote "Take project.stage from the config block above ... Map its value to a catalog phase key." That content is not there. It is actually at line 70 ("1. **Take `project.stage` from the config block above** — it is already resolved. Map its value to a catalog phase key:") followed by the 7-row Concept->...->Release table at lines 71-77. Lines 96-105 cover Step 3 (reading production/session-state/active.md) and the opening of Step 4 (artifact-based checks) — unrelated content with no mention of project.stage or the phase-key mapping. The same wrong range (96-105) is reused in the top-level 'silent_breaks' entry for the two-track finding, so the error propagates into the assessment's marquee 'verified by direct read, not inferred' claim.
issues.failure_scenario: A reader opens help/SKILL.md at lines 96-105 to verify the hardcoded-mapping claim, finds Step 3/4 content instead, and either wrongly concludes the claim is fabricated or has to re-locate the real evidence themselves — undermining trust in the one deliverable-1 finding the assessment stresses is directly verified rather than inferred.
issues.correction: Cite line 70 (and 71-77 for the mapping table) instead of 96-105. The underlying claim — that /help hardcodes a single project.stage-to-phase-key table and therefore can't natively represent two concurrent tracks — is itself correct; only the line citation is wrong.

issues.problem: DELIVERABLE 1 SUMMARY states the catalog's 7 phases run "concept(5 steps)->systems-design(4)->technical-setup(5)->pre-production(11)->production(9)->polish(5)->release(4)". Counting the actual `- id:` step entries per phase in the file gives concept=6, systems-design=4, technical-setup=5, pre-production=10, production=11, polish=5, release=4 (45 steps total, not the ~43 implied by the assessment's numbers). Three of the seven per-phase counts are wrong: concept is understated by 1, pre-production is overstated by 1, and production is understated by 2.
issues.failure_scenario: Someone sizing the firm-setup track's step count (e.g. to estimate effort per phase, or to check that a rewritten catalog preserves step counts) trusts the assessment's numbers and under-scopes concept and production while over-scoping pre-production.
issues.correction: Correct the phase step-counts to concept=6, pre-production=10, production=11 (systems-design/technical-setup/polish/release, at 4/5/5/4, were already right).

issues.problem: The assessment states T2 verdicts as flat, confidently-formatted facts for four components that have NO corresponding row in scratchpad/mapping.txt, the file this verification pass was told to check divergent verdicts against: (1) .claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml — "t2_verdict":"W (phase names + artifact paths renamed; structure kept)"; (2) CCGS Skill Testing Framework/catalog.yaml — "K (mechanism kept); W (T2, content renamed)"; (3) CCGS Skill Testing Framework/quality-rubric.md — "K (mechanism); content renamed per-category for T2"; (4) the bundled "static/spec/category/audit modes" row — "static:K/audit:degrades/spec:breaks/category:breaks (same for T2 per README's mode table)". I checked all 39 top-level templates + 7 guidance files + 13 rules against mapping.txt's t1/t2 columns and every single one matches exactly, which shows mapping.txt genuinely was the source used for those 59 rows. The 4 rows above are presented in the identical confident format but are untraceable to that source and are not marked INFERENCE anywhere.
issues.failure_scenario: A reader treats these 4 T2-verdict claims (e.g. 'T2's catalog.yaml keeps the mechanism and only renames content') as equally verified as the other 59 that do check out against mapping.txt, when in fact there is no record anywhere in scope of what T2 actually did with these files — mapping.txt is silent on all of them (grep confirms zero hits for 'catalog.yaml', 'quality-rubric', 'CCGS Skill Testing Framework', and 'workflow-catalog.yaml' as a component row).
issues.correction: Either cite the actual source for these 4 T2-verdict claims, or relabel them explicitly as INFERENCE (a plausible extrapolation from T2's general 'mechanism kept, content renamed' pattern seen elsewhere) so they are not mistaken for mapping.txt-sourced facts.

issues.problem: The task's scope statement for the area explicitly lists "templates/" as part of the in-scope CCGS Skill Testing Framework content. `ls` confirms this directory contains exactly two files: skill-test-spec.md and agent-test-spec.md. Neither file appears anywhere in the assessment's components list, evidence array, findings, or reuse_patterns — they are never opened, quoted, or given a verdict, not even folded into the bundled 'static/spec/category/audit modes' entry by name.
issues.failure_scenario: Under Strategy C ("transplant operating foundation ... write domain agents/skills fresh"), these two files are exactly what a new HF skill/agent behavioral spec would be authored from (I confirmed skill-test-spec.md is a fully domain-neutral authoring template — category enum, static assertions, director-gate checks, test-case skeleton). A founder or engineer relying on this assessment as the transplant manifest would not know these templates exist or need a verdict, and would either rediscover them from scratch or miss them entirely when rewriting the 123-name registry.
issues.correction: Add skill-test-spec.md and agent-test-spec.md as their own components (or explicitly fold them into the existing catalog/rubric/mode-table entry) with a stated verdict and at least one evidence citation, since they are named in-scope and were apparently never read.

verify.overall: The assessment is largely well-supported: of roughly 62 evidence citations I opened and checked against actual file content (well over the required 20, spanning workflow-catalog.yaml, all 39 top-level templates, all 7 guidance files, all 13 rules, and the CCGS Skill Testing Framework's catalog.yaml/quality-rubric.md/README.md), only one is materially wrong -- and it happens to back the assessment's single most-stressed 'verified by direct read, not inferred' claim (help/SKILL.md cited at lines 96-105, actually at line 70). Verdict-logic cross-checking against scratchpad/mapping.txt was strong where mapping.txt actually has data: all 39 template t2_verdicts, all 7 guidance-file t2_verdicts, and all 13 rule t2_verdicts I checked match mapping.txt exactly, and the divergent-from-T2 rationales I stress-tested (data-files.md, gameplay-code.md, ADR family) hold up reasonably for a regulated hedge fund. Coverage of the 46 templates and 13 rules is complete -- I found no missing template or rule. The real problems are: (1) the wrong help/SKILL.md line citation noted above; (2) three wrong per-phase step counts in the DELIVERABLE 1 SUMMARY (concept and production undercounted, pre-production overcounted); (3) four T2-verdict claims (workflow-catalog.yaml, and three CCGS-framework rows) presented with the same confident sourcing as the other 59 but with zero corresponding entry anywhere in mapping.txt, and not flagged as INFERENCE; and (4) two in-scope files (CCGS Skill Testing Framework/templates/skill-test-spec.md and agent-test-spec.md) that the assessment never examines or cites despite the task scope naming 'templates/' explicitly. None of these change the assessment's overall thesis, but the wrong citation and the unsourced T2 verdicts should be fixed before the document is used as the basis for founder-facing transplant decisions.
